  "claims": [
    {"id":"f1","concept_id":"c1","text":"A checkpoint transfers WAL transactions back into the original database.","source_id":"S1","quote":"Moving the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a \" checkpoint \".","pass":0},
    {"id":"f2","concept_id":"c2","text":"sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) triggers checkpointing after a commit when the WAL contains at least N frames.","source_id":"S3","quote":"automatically checkpoint after committing a transaction if there are N or more frames in the write-ahead log file.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f3","concept_id":"c2","text":"Checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint are PASSIVE.","source_id":"S3","quote":"Checkpoints initiated by this mechanism are PASSIVE . Every new database connection defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled","pass":0},
    {"id":"f4","concept_id":"c3","text":"A checkpoint must stop at a WAL page past any current reader's end mark.","source_id":"S1","quote":"the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f5","concept_id":"c5","text":"Checkpointing normally does not truncate the WAL file, with journal_size_limit identified as an exception.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set).","pass":0},
    {"id":"f6","concept_id":"c6","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE checkpoints as many frames as possible without waiting for readers or writers to finish.","source_id":"S2","quote":"Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish, then sync the database file if all frames in the log were checkpointed.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f7","concept_id":"c7","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL waits until there is no writer and all readers use the most recent database snapshot.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback ) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f8","concept_id":"c4","text":"The WAL must be synced to persistent storage before checkpoint content moves into the database.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database","pass":0},

    {"id":"f9","concept_id":"c4","text":"The database file must be synced before the WAL is reset.","source_id":"S1","quote":"the database and the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f10","concept_id":"c3","text":"The reader end-mark boundary prevents checkpointing from overwriting database content a reader is actively using.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The checkpoint has to stop at that point because otherwise it might overwrite part of the database file that the reader is actively using.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f11","concept_id":"c3","text":"The checkpoint records its progress in the wal-index so the next invocation resumes where it stopped.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The checkpoint remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got and will resume transferring content from the WAL to the database from where it left off on the next invocation.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f12","concept_id":"c8","text":"After checkpointing, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART additionally waits until all readers read only from the database file.","source_id":"S2","quote":"after checkpointing the log file it blocks (calls the busy-handler callback ) until all readers are reading from the database file only.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f13","concept_id":"c8","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART ensures that the next writer restarts the WAL from its beginning.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f14","concept_id":"c9","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE adds truncation of the log to zero bytes immediately before successful return to RESTART behavior.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f15","concept_id":"c10","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP always checkpoints zero frames.","source_id":"S2","quote":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned","pass":1},
    {"id":"f16","concept_id":"c6","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE never invokes the busy-handler callback.","source_id":"S2","quote":"The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode. On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished","pass":1},
    {"id":"f17","concept_id":"c7","text":"A pending SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL blocks new database writers.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f18","concept_id":"c7","text":"A pending SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL allows new database readers to continue unimpeded.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.","pass":1},

    {"id":"f19","concept_id":"c13","text":"If overlapping readers always leave at least one reader active, checkpoints cannot complete and the WAL grows without bound.","source_id":"S1","quote":"if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.","pass":2},
    {"id":"f20","concept_id":"c11","text":"A checkpoint returns SQLITE_BUSY if another checkpoint prevents acquisition of the exclusive checkpoint lock.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned.","pass":2},
    {"id":"f21","concept_id":"c11","text":"Checkpoint-lock contention does not invoke a configured busy-handler.","source_id":"S2","quote":"the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.","pass":2},
    {"id":"f22","concept_id":"c11","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE also acquire the exclusive writer lock.","source_id":"S2","quote":"The SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE modes also obtain the exclusive \"writer\" lock on the database file.","pass":2},
    {"id":"f23","concept_id":"c12","text":"If the busy-handler returns zero before writer-lock acquisition or while waiting for readers, checkpointing continues with PASSIVE behavior.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If the busy-handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE","pass":2},
    {"id":"f24","concept_id":"c12","text":"Busy-handler refusal followed by PASSIVE fallback returns SQLITE_BUSY.","source_id":"S2","quote":"checkpointing as many frames as possible without blocking any further. SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case.","pass":2},
    {"id":"f25","concept_id":"c2","text":"Passing N less than or equal to zero to sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint disables automatic checkpoints.","source_id":"S3","quote":"Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.","pass":2},
    {"id":"f26","concept_id":"c2","text":"Registering a callback with sqlite3_wal_hook disables automatic checkpointing configured through sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint.","source_id":"S3","quote":"Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by this function.","pass":2},
    {"id":"f27","concept_id":"c4","text":"With PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, checkpointing is the only operation that issues an I/O barrier or sync.","source_id":"S1","quote":"Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation","pass":2},
    {"id":"f28","concept_id":"c14","text":"With PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL and checkpoints in a separate thread or process, the main query-and-update thread or process never blocks on a sync operation.","source_id":"S1","quote":"If an application therefore runs checkpoint in a separate thread or process, the main thread or process that is doing database queries and updates will never block on a sync operation.","pass":2},

    {"id":"f29","concept_id":"c4","text":"The described synchronous=NORMAL configuration with separate checkpoint execution permits transactions to roll back after power failure or hard reset.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The downside to this configuration is that transactions are no longer durable and might rollback following a power failure or hard reset.","pass":3},
    {"id":"f30","concept_id":"c5","text":"A writer rewinds the WAL when all WAL content has been transferred and synced and no readers are using the WAL.","source_id":"S1","quote":"if the entire WAL has been transferred into the database and synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL, then the writer will rewind the WAL back to the beginning","pass":3},
    {"id":"f31","concept_id":"c16","text":"Starting with SQLite 3.11.0, dated 2016-02-15, a single transaction's WAL should be proportional in size to that transaction.","source_id":"S1","quote":"As of SQLite version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15), the WAL file for a single transaction should be proportional in size to the transaction itself.","pass":3},
    {"id":"f32","concept_id":"c16","text":"Before SQLite 3.11.0, a transaction larger than the page cache could write the same page into the WAL multiple times.","source_id":"S1","quote":"However, with older versions of SQLite, the same page might be written into the WAL file multiple times if the transaction grows larger than the page cache.","pass":3},
    {"id":"f33","concept_id":"c15","text":"pnCkpt counts checkpointed frames already present before the current function call, rather than only work performed by that call.","source_id":"S2","quote":"the total number of checkpointed frames in the log file (including any that were already checkpointed before the function was called)","pass":3},
    {"id":"f34","concept_id":"c15","text":"For a named attached database outside WAL mode, sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 returns SQLITE_OK and sets pnLog and pnCkpt to -1.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If database zDb is the name of an attached database that is not in WAL mode, SQLITE_OK is returned and both *pnLog and *pnCkpt set to -1.","pass":3},
    {"id":"f35","concept_id":"c14","text":"By default, the thread performing the COMMIT that crosses the WAL size limit also performs the automatic checkpoint.","source_id":"S1","quote":"By default, the checkpoint will be run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit.","pass":3},
    {"id":"f36","concept_id":"c16","text":"The WAL cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.","source_id":"S1","quote":"A checkpoint can only complete when no other transactions are running, which means the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.","pass":3}

claims.text: The WAL cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.

limitations: Only S1, S2 and S3 were used. No tools, external research, runtime execution or persistent changes were performed.

The six questions were applied to accumulated claims: mechanism, boundaries, exceptions and primary-source wording yielded facts; history yielded the SQLite 3.11.0 change; the packet supplies no independent expert disagreement.

S1 lists three checkpoint subtypes and mentions RESET, whereas S2 explicitly documents five modes including TRUNCATE and NOOP. The packet does not establish the chronology or explain this documentation discrepancy.
S1 broadly warns that RESTART and TRUNCATE might block readers; S2 describes RESTART as not impeding readers. The packet does not establish the conditions that reconcile these statements.
Historical evidence is limited to the large-transaction change dated 2016-02-15; broader checkpoint evolution and paraphrase drift cannot be established.
The hard budget ended after three deepening passes at a new-information rate of 22.2222%. No two consecutive passes fell below 5%, so depth saturation was not demonstrated.

The 36-claim output cap leaves supplied details unenumerated, including attached-database iteration, additional status semantics and reader-gap mitigation. At least one further pass appears useful; the evidence does not justify a precise estimate beyond that.
